text: Radahn's mind was destroyed by scarlet rot infection after Malenia released the Scarlet Bloom during the Battle of Aeonia.

During the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia's needle broke—whether by accident or choice remains ambiguous—unleashing the scarlet rot she had suppressed since birth as the Scarlet Bloom (Scarlet Aeonia), a massive crimson flower that destroyed Caelid, transforming it into a permanent blood-red rotted wasteland.

After the war against the Fire Giants ended with no worthy opponents remaining, Marika deliberately stripped Godfrey and his warriors/kinfolk of their grace, exiling them beyond the Lands Between (across the Sea of Fog to the Badlands, in what became known as the Long March), commanding them to become the first Tarnished and wage war.
Godfrey was the first human Marika chose as her consort and the warrior who led the campaigns expanding the Erdtree's dominion across the Lands Between.
Messmer was sent to the Land of Shadow to wage a campaign of conquest and was then forgotten, his name removed from records.
The Black Knife Assassins are the Numen women who carried out the Night of the Black Knives, which killed Godwyn, after being subverted by Ranni.

Guardians protecting the passage to the deep root depths, and through it Godwyn's resting place, stand between the ordinary world and the aftermath of the Night of the Black Knives, the event in which Godwyn was killed.
The Scadutree Avatar's guardianship predates the current age, dating to a time before the Erdtree dominated, when the Shadow Tree's realm was simply the world rather than a hidden counterpart.

Marika directed Godfrey to wage war against the Fire Giants because their flame of ruin threatened the Erdtree; this campaign, the defining war of the early Golden Order, nearly annihilated the giants entirely.
The Nox were punished for a rebellion against the Greater Will, their cities forced underground as a form of exile.

The people of the eternal cities (sometimes called the 'Dox' people) were once the most advanced scholars of the Lands Between, studying stars and cosmic forces and building underground cities lit by artificial constellations, before being punished for rebelling against the Greater Will by having their entire civilization buried underground.
Miquella later attempted to use the same Gate of Divinity at Anor Ilim to claim his own godhood, as depicted in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.
Marika summoned Radagon back to the Erdtree capital to become her second Elden Lord consort, ending his marriage to Renala, and together they had the twins Miquella and Malenia.
entities: Renala, Queen of the Full Moon

text: Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring is portrayed as a deliberate act by a god who no longer believed in the system she built, not an accident or madness.

Godfrey fought and made peace with some ancient dragons, defeated the Storm Lord in single combat (an event still echoed in Stormveil Castle's architecture), and led wars expanding the Golden Order's influence, including against the Fire Giants.
One Fire Giant was deliberately spared and cursed/chained at the Mountaintops of the Giants to keep a forge flame—too strong for Marika to extinguish—burning for future use in opening the Erdtree.
Marika promised the exiled Tarnished that after death she would eventually return their grace and give them a chance to return and serve as Elden Lord.
Radagon's previous marriage to Renala, Queen of the Full Moon of the Carian royal family, was a political alliance between the Golden Order and the Carian sorcerers.
entities: Renala, Queen of the Full Moon

text: The opening narration states that on a night of wintry fog, the Rune of Death was stolen and the demigods began to fall, starting with Godwyn the Golden.

Ranni the Witch rejected her fate of being controlled by the Two Fingers and masterminded the Night of the Black Knives, stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and forging/imbuing it into the Black Knife Assassins' blades.
On the Night of the Black Knives, assassins killed Godwyn the Golden using a fragment of the stolen Rune of Death, carving a death curse mark intended to fully erase both body and soul.

At the exact moment Godwyn died, Ranni took her own life at the top of a high, isolated tower, splitting the death curse mark into two half-circles instead of one complete circle—one half carved into Godwyn's flesh, the other half carried by Ranni's discarded body.
The knife that killed Godwyn only carried a fragment of the Rune of Death, so it killed only his soul, leaving his body alive but soulless.
Godwyn's soulless body grew and festered within the underground roots beneath Leyndell, becoming the entity known as the Prince of Death.
Ranni's body died but her soul survived because she had planned for this outcome in advance.
Ranni transferred her soul into a small doll modeled after a mentor she had loved and lost—the Snow Witch Renna—then vanished from the world's awareness.
To escape the Two Fingers' control, Ranni needed to die in the flesh while preserving her soul, which the Knight of the Black Knives' stolen Rune of Death made possible.
Godwyn's death was the first death of a demigod in the history of the Lands Between.
Godwyn the Golden's death was the most devastating loss to Marika from the coordinated assassinations, since he embodied everything she hoped the Golden Order could produce.
Ranni, Marika's stepdaughter, used a piece of Marika's own system to murder Marika's firstborn son Godwyn.

Following Godwyn's death, Marika took the Elden Ring and shattered it, breaking the fundamental laws of reality and resulting in her own imprisonment within the Erdtree, which triggered the war among the demigods known as the Shattering.
The shards of the shattered Elden Ring flew outward and settled in or near Marika's demigod children, becoming corrupting Great Runes whose power triggered the war known as the Shattering.
Radahn halted the stars specifically to prevent Ranni's planned Age of Stars from occurring, since her destiny required the stars to fall.
When Radahn was defeated at the Radahn Festival, the stars he held moved and a fragment struck the earth, opening the previously inaccessible underground city of Nokron.
Nokron's opening was specifically what Ranni needed for the next stage of her plan.
Malenia marched her army from the Haligtree south to fight Radahn in the Battle of Aeonia, the defining conflict of the Shattering.
Malenia's Cleanrot Knights, who accepted exposure to scarlet rot out of loyalty, fought Radahn's soldiers in one of the bloodiest battles in Lands Between history.
Malenia and Radahn were evenly matched in personal combat, as neither had ever lost a battle before.
Radahn's loyal soldiers organized the Radahn Festival, inviting warriors worldwide to give their general an honorable death in battle rather than kill him for conquest.
After the battle, Malenia fell into a deep, dreamless coma.
A Cleanrot Knight named Finlay carried Malenia's unconscious body alone back to the Haligtree, fighting off enemies the entire way.
After the Shattering ended with no victor, the demigods retreated to their strongholds and Leyndell remained mostly intact but without a true Elden Lord.
Malenia sleeps in the depths of Elphael, the branch of the Haligtree, waiting for Miquella to return.
Even during Malenia's sleep, the scarlet rot she carries continues to spread and corrupt the Haligtree, which Miquella intended as a pure sanctuary.
Miquella grew the Haligtree from a sapling, watering it with his own Empyrean blood hoping his growth would be reflected in the tree, but it never became a full Erdtree.
While Malenia was fighting Radahn, Mohg, Lord of Blood, kidnapped the sleeping Miquella and took him to his hidden palace underground.

Mohg wrapped Miquella in a cocoon of golden silk and fed him blood in a ritual meant to elevate Miquella to divine status, trying to rouse him with offerings and shared bedchambers, though Miquella never woke.
Through symbolic death in Mohg's cocoon, Miquella broke free of the Erdtree's death-rebirth cycle and shed his flesh piece by piece on his path to the Gate of Divinity.

When Mohg stood before (or encountered while imprisoned) the Formless Mother, an outer god, his cursed/crucible-marked blood caught fire, and the deity chose him as her vessel, granting him bloodflame incantations.
The Fell God is the ancient fire deity of the giants that Marika and Godfrey went to war against in the early days of the Golden Order.
When Godfrey destroyed nearly all the giants, the Fell God lost most of its followers but did not die, and still lurks in the Mountaintops of the Giants.
Vyke took the Frenzied Flame into himself to save his finger maiden from being sacrificed to burn open the Erdtree.
Vyke became a Lord of Frenzy and lost his path to the throne, wandering into madness.
Ranni seeks the Finger-Slayer Blade, hidden in the underground city of Nokron, to pursue her plan involving the Dark Moon.
The Finger-Slayer Blade was made in Nokron by a people who had rebelled against the Greater Will and were punished for it.
Ranni travels to the Moonlight Altar, a remote plateau guarded by a sleeping ancient dragon coiled around a cathedral of sorcery, to claim a special ring meant for her Elden Lord consort.
Ranni leaves the Dark Moon Ring for the tarnished to retrieve and bring back to her, formally asking them to be her lord and consort.
The Shattering was a devastating war between the demigod children of Queen Marika, sparked when the shattering of the Elden Ring caused open war among them, breaking the empire into fragments.
On a night of wintry fog, a group of unknown assassins struck across the Lands Between, killing many of Queen Marika's kin.

No single faction in the Shattering could achieve decisive victory even when empowered by a Great Rune; the battle between General Radahn and Malenia the Severed, which had no victor, demonstrated that neither could conquer all the lands united by Marika, and the Lands Between settled into an unresolved stalemate rather than open war.
The Shattering meant abandonment of the Lands Between by the Greater Will.
Marika ordered Maliketh to lock away the Rune of Death, also called Destined Death.
To prevent the Rune of Death from being stolen again, Maliketh bound his sword, imbued with the rune, within his own body and changed his name.
After Malenia's Scarlet Aeonia bloomed in Caelid during the Shattering, Gowry dedicated his services to her, believing she would found a new Order of Rot.
Shabriri was also the name of a man punished for slander by having his eyes gouged out, after which his eyes filled with the flame of frenzy.
According to the Howl of Shabriri, this was the first instance of the maddening sickness of frenzy in the Lands Between.
Kale's nomadic clan, the Great Caravan, was accused of heresy and buried alive underground, where they summoned the flame of frenzy.
General Radahn recruited Jerren into his army as a guest commander during the Shattering, before he could fulfill his promise to slay Sellen.
Tanith worked as a dancer in an unnamed foreign land until she caught Rykard's eye and became his consort, and he brought her back to the Lands Between.
As an Empyrean, Queen Marika was given Maliketh as a Shadow and half-brother, to whom she entrusted the Rune of Death when the Golden Order was established.
Queen Marika's first consort was Godfrey, with whom she had three children: Godwyn the Golden and the Omen twins Morgott and Mohg.

On behalf of the Greater Will, Marika and her followers waged wars to spread the Golden Order's influence, most notably against the Storm Lord, the fire giants and their god the One-Eyed God, and the Academy of Raya Lucaria and Carian royal family.
It is unclear which side instigated the wars against the Dragons and against the Godskin Apostles and their god, the Gloam-Eyed Queen.
Marika tasked Radagon with leading the Erdtree's armies in the war against Liurnia of the Lakes.
Sword monuments in Liurnia suggest there were two Liurnian Wars, and during or after the second, Radagon and Rennala met in battle and fell in love.
Radagon sought absolution at the Church of Vows using Celestial Dew, and he and Rennala were married there, uniting Leyndell and the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Radagon and Rennala had three children together: General Radahn, Praetor Rykard, and Lunar Princess Ranni.
Radagon gifted Rennala an Amber Egg and left her to rejoin Marika's side when Godfrey and his fellow Tarnished were exiled.
Despite being the same person, Marika and Radagon held different wills; when Marika shattered the Elden Ring, Radagon used the same hammer to try to repair it.
As chieftain of the badlands, Hoarah Loux was a fierce warrior with strong bloodlust before being selected as Marika's consort.
During Godfrey's reign, gladiatorial combat in colosseums across the Lands Between was common as rituals honoring the Erdtree, a practice that ended when Radagon became Marika's consort.
Godfrey's axe was broken in battle during the Long March, and after the journey he reverted to being a simple warrior while still carrying Serosh on his back.
Rennala's mastery of lunar magic allowed her to become head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and its Glintstone Knights, and to establish the Carian family as royalty.
One night, Rennala took her daughter Ranni out stargazing as she had done in her own childhood, which led to Ranni meeting her own moon, the Dark Moon.
When Godfrey was exiled and Radagon returned to Marika's side, Rennala was devastated and grew weak, losing her charm over the Academy.
The Academy's scholars rebelled against the Carian royal family, with the Cuckoo Knights attacking Caria Manor and locking Rennala in the Grand Library.
Royal-blooded Omens, including Morgott and Mohg, were hidden from the world and shackled in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell.
During the Shattering, when Leyndell was leaderless, Morgott secretly ruled the capital as the Unveiled Monarch, knowing it wouldn't accept an Omen as leader.
During the Second Defense of Leyndell, Morgott successfully defended the capital and the Erdtree from invading demigods.
Mohg eventually escaped the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and established Mohgwyn Palace in a secluded part of the Siofra River.
The ancient people of Mt. Gelmir worshipped a powerful serpent god, offering it sacrifices.
Rykard encountered the God-Devouring Serpent and offered himself and his Great Rune as sacrifices to gain immortality, allowing him to grow and devour people and gods for eternity.
Rykard's fall into greed and gluttony caused most of his followers to turn against him, with Tanith remaining a notable exception.

Former Gelmir Knights sought out the great spear Serpent-Hunter, designed to kill the immortal God-Devouring Serpent, to stop Rykard, but were unsuccessful, as evidenced by corpses found holding the weapon in his boss room.

Messmer the Impaler was tasked with purging the tower-dwelling Hornsent, known as Omens in the Lands Between and representing an older religion predating Marika's rule, and he and his forces decimated their people.
Leda hints at a tumultuous past between the Hornsent and the tower folk, resulting from ancient conflicts instigated by Queen Marika's commands.
The Dragon Communion Priestess provides lore about Bayle and Placidusax, revealing the former dominion and decline of the Ancient Dragons.
